You are a teaching assistant for Biology for Engineers. You have pure-breeding wheat plants of a particular kind which produce long and thin seeds (Dominant, LLTT). You also have pure-breeding plants of short and thick seeds (ttll). You asked your student project assistant to cross the two and to give you the results of F1. Unfortunately, your student forgets to record the phenotype of the F1 plants in her notebook, though she does remember that they all looked the same. The F1 was test crossed and the results are:

Long wheat, thick seeds = 186

Long wheat, thin seeds = 564

Short wheat, thick seeds = 63

Short wheat, thin seeds = 187

1. Construct a Punnett square explaining the test cross.

2. Calculate the recombination frequency.

3. What is your conclusion from the results of test cross?

In 1796, Edward Jenner, an English physician noticed that dairy workers who had caught relatively mild disease cowpox from cows seemed to be immune to smallpox. He found that rubbing pus from cowpox sores into scratches in the skin prevented people from coming down with smallpox later. Almost a century later, Louis Pasteur found a safer way to prepare vaccines. He discovered how to attenuate (kill them so that they will infect, but no disease is caused) microorganisms until they could no longer cause disease. Smallpox was not only the first disease to be prevented by vaccination but also the first disease to be officially eradicated by human efforts.

i) How does vaccination protect the body from getting disease?

ii) Is it safe to use attenuated microorganisms as vaccines?

iii) Explain why rubbing pus from cowpox sores into scratches in the skin prevented people from getting smallpox.

iv) Give the reason why several diseases such as common cold, chicken pox, corona etc have remained ineffective or partially effective against vaccines.

(1+1+1+1 = 4 marks)
